key_insight: Using deployment-specific context available before generation can help predict whether clinicians will reject an LLM response, outperforming query content alone.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support targeted guardrails or abstention in clinical LLM tools, making them safer and more aligned with real workflow use.
method: Trained a pre-response classifier to estimate rejection risk before the LLM generates an answer.
Used query content plus deployment context such as provider type, department, and model used.
Evaluated prospectively over 4.5 months of sparse real-world user feedback.
evidence_signal: In a prospective deployment-centered evaluation, the rejection-risk model achieved an AUROC of 0.719.
watch_item: The model is based on sparse feedback from one academic medical center, so performance and utility may not generalize across settings or user groups.
paper_title: Deployment-Centered Evaluation: Predicting Query-Level Rejection Risk in a Clinical LLM System
